name: ESSAI 2026
venue: European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence, Vienna, Austria
description: The 4th European Summer School on Artificial Intelligence (ESSAI) will be held in Vienna, Austria from 6 to 10 July 2026, targeting PhD students and young researchers in AI. It offers a one‑week intensive program with introductory and advanced courses, specialized tutorials on Bilateral AI and Digital Humanism, and a rich social programme including a reception at the Vienna City Hall. The school is co‑located with the 5th ACM Europe Digital Humanism Summer School and features over 30 lecturers across six parallel tracks.

name: OpenEuroLLM Winter School
venue: Skeikampen conference hotel, near Oslo, Norway
description: The 2026 Winter School on Multilinguality in LLM Development and Evaluation is held at the Skeikampen conference hotel north of Oslo, Norway. It targets NLP researchers, especially those from EuroHPC countries and doctoral candidates, and offers technical talks, hands‑on sessions, and reflections on large‑scale multilingual language models. The event is fully subsidised by the OpenEuroLLM project, includes free bus transfers from Oslo Airport, and provides a mountain‑side setting with skiing and walking opportunities.

name: Probabilistic AI School
description: The Probabilistic AI School 2026 will take place in Vilnius, Lithuania. The school aims to provide an inclusive educational environment covering state‑of‑the‑art machine‑learning and artificial‑intelligence topics. It welcomes students, academics, industry professionals and AI enthusiasts to participate in lectures and workshops.

name: BMVA Computer Vision Summer School
description: The 29th BMVA Computer Vision Summer School will be held at Durham University in Durham, England, UK. It offers an intensive week of lectures and lab sessions covering a wide range of computer‑vision topics, delivered by leading researchers from the UK and abroad. The programme features daily oral talks and hands‑on sessions designed for students and researchers seeking advanced training in the field.

name: Oxford Machine Learning Summer School 2026
venue: Oxford Machine Learning School, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The Oxford Machine Learning School offers a Summer 2026 program both on‑site in Oxford and online. Participants can select from three specialised tracks covering the latest AI theory, applications, and frontier foundation models, learning from world‑renowned experts in academia and industry. The curriculum is fully customisable, allowing attendees to combine tracks to match their individual learning goals.

name: Robotics, Perception and Learning (RPL) Summer School
venue: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, Stockholm, Sweden
description: The RPL Summer School 2026, organized by the Department for Robotics, Perception and Learning at KTH Royal Institute of Technology, brings together doctoral and postdoctoral researchers in Stockholm, Sweden. It covers a broad spectrum of topics such as machine learning, computer vision, robotics, human‑robot interaction, planning and decision making through keynotes, industry talks, and interactive brainstorming sessions. The six‑day program aims to foster new collaborations by combining academic and industrial perspectives in a relaxed setting with indoor and outdoor activities.

name: Machine Learning Crash Course at MALGA
description: The MLCC2026 Summer School – Machine Learning Crash Course – provides an introduction to fundamental machine‑learning concepts and algorithms. It is aimed at undergraduate and graduate students, as well as professionals, and is open to participants from any university after a selection process. The five‑day in‑person program in Genoa combines theoretical lectures with hands‑on lab sessions and includes a final test consisting of notebook work and a report.

name: UK Robotics Summer School
venue: National Robotarium, Heriot-Watt University, Edinburgh, United Kingdom
description: The UK Robotics Summer School 2026 is a five‑day event held at the National Robotarium, Heriot‑Watt University in Edinburgh, United Kingdom. It offers expert‑led lectures, tutorials and industry talks covering bio‑inspired robotics, healthcare robotics, generative AI for robotics, safe AI and real‑world applications, with hands‑on experience using state‑of‑the‑art technology. The programme targets master’s‑level students and industry practitioners, providing networking opportunities with academics and industry leaders.

name: International Summer School for Advanced Studies on Biometrics, Behavior, and Vision
description: The 2026 Biometrics Summer School takes place in Alghero, Sardinia, Italy, hosted at the Hotel Dei Pini. It focuses on the impact of generative AI and large foundation models on biometric and human‑recognition technologies, covering machine learning, image understanding, signal analysis, neuroscience, robotics, forensic and digital forensics. The program is aimed at PhD students, post‑docs, researchers and professionals, offering intensive lectures by 20 international experts, hands‑on sessions, and the possibility of scholarships and a short‑paper presentation.

name: Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal (ELS) aspects of AI and AS at Umeå University
description: The Winter School on Ethical, Legal, and Societal aspects of AI and Autonomous Systems brings together researchers and students to explore the broader implications of emerging technologies. It offers a mix of lectures, hands‑on multidisciplinary training, a poster session, and a social program to foster networking and professional exchange. The event takes place at Umeå University in Sweden, providing participants with access to university facilities and nearby accommodation options.

name: Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia (SoRAIM 2026)
description: The SoRAIM’27 Winter School on Social Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Multimedia brings together researchers interested in social robotics and socially intelligent systems. It targets PhD students and early‑career researchers, offering lectures, hands‑on sessions and informal networking in a mountain setting near Grenoble. The programme aims to foster cross‑disciplinary exchange across computer vision, speech processing, affective computing and human‑robot interaction, while providing opportunities for collaboration and outdoor activities.

name: Northern Lights Deep Learning Winter School
venue: UiT The Arctic University of Norway, Tromsø, Norway
description: The 2027 NLDL Winter School is part of the Northern Lights Deep Learning Conference and will be held in Tromsø, Norway. It runs from 11 to 15 January and offers intensive training on state-of-the-art deep‑learning methods such as image classification, object detection, segmentation, time‑series prediction and speech recognition. The school targets researchers and practitioners who want to learn cutting‑edge techniques and foster collaborations within the international deep‑learning community.

name: Annual Nepal AI School (ANAIS)
description: The 7th Annual Nepal AI School is an 11‑day intensive program held in Kathmandu, Nepal, offering lectures, labs, and project work on artificial intelligence. It targets senior undergraduates, graduate students, PhD candidates, faculty members, and industry professionals, covering topics from fundamental mathematics to cutting‑edge areas such as geometric deep learning, world models, generative modeling, and neuro‑symbolic AI. The school aims to build AI expertise in the region, foster collaboration among international researchers, and inspire the next generation of AI leaders.

name: EEML Summer School
description: The Eastern European Machine Learning Summer School takes place in Cetinje, Montenegro from 27 July to 1 August 2026. The program features lectures and tutorials by leading researchers from institutions such as Google DeepMind, MIT, and the University of Cambridge, covering a broad range of machine‑learning topics. It is aimed at students and early‑career researchers in Eastern Europe who want to deepen their knowledge and network with experts in the field.

name: Mediterranean Summer School
description: The Mediterranean Machine Learning (M2L) Summer School is a five‑day event that brings together AI experts to deliver keynotes, lectures, and hands‑on sessions. It targets doctoral and outstanding master students, as well as academics and practitioners, focusing on topics such as computer vision, NLP, generative models, reinforcement learning and ethics. The 2027 edition will be held in Spain in September, offering networking opportunities, poster presentations, and scholarships to promote diversity.

name: Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI
venue: Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications, Rabat, Morocco
description: The AI Summer School on Multimodal Foundation Models and Generative AI is a five‑day program held at the Institut National des Postes et Télécommunications in Rabat, Morocco. It targets master’s, Ph.D., post‑doc and early‑career researchers as well as industry professionals, offering lectures, hands‑on labs, and project mentorship on state‑of‑the‑art multimodal and generative AI techniques. The school combines expert instruction from leading AI scientists with networking events to build a community of AI leaders in Morocco.

name: AthNLP Summer School 2026
description: The Athens Natural Language Processing Summer School 2026 (AthNLP) will be held at the campus of NCSR Demokritos in Athens, Greece. It offers intensive training on NLP topics and is organized jointly by several research institutions, including RC Athena, NCSR Demokritos, Athens University of Economics and Business, Heriot-Watt University, and the ELLIS‑University of Manchester partnership. The program runs from September 2 to September 8, 2026, and also supports the 14th EETN Conference on Artificial Intelligence taking place immediately afterwards.

name: Advanced Artificial Intelligence: GenAI & Deep Unsupervised Learning
venue: Lady Margaret Hall, Oxford, United Kingdom
description: The Advanced Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning summer school at Lady Margaret Hall focuses on generative AI and deep unsupervised learning techniques. It combines theoretical lectures with hands‑on projects covering clustering, GANs, self‑supervised learning, and their real‑world applications across various domains. The programme is aimed at STEM students with intermediate AI/ML experience and is offered as a residential or online course.

name: AI4Science Summer School
description: The 2nd Summer School on Advancing Scientific Discovery with AI brings together researchers, PhD students and post‑doctoral scholars to explore how artificial intelligence can accelerate scientific research. The program covers machine‑learning for data analysis, AI‑driven experimental design, generative models, and integration of AI with physical simulations, featuring hands‑on workshops using Python libraries such as NumPy and PyTorch. Emphasizing interdisciplinary collaboration, the school aims to equip participants with practical skills to apply deep‑learning techniques to their own scientific problems.

name: LUT Summer School
description: LUT Summer School is a one‑week intensive program offering courses on sustainability, climate action, marketing, management, and the intersection of business and technology. It is aimed at bachelor’s and master’s students who enroll in a short exchange, with each course worth 3 ECTS credits and featuring workshops, group work, and a social programme in Finnish nature. The courses take place on the Lappeenranta campus from 3 to 7 August 2026 and include both on‑site teaching and optional online components.

name: 1st Internationa School on the Cognitive, Ethical, and Societal Dimensions of AI - AIces
description: The AIces 2026 International School focuses on the cognitive, ethical and societal dimensions of artificial intelligence. It is aimed at graduate and postgraduate students, as well as industry practitioners, offering parallel courses, a symposium, and open debates. The event takes place in Porto, Portugal from 30 March to 2 April 2026, with both face‑to‑face interaction and live online participation, and recordings available for 45 days after the school.
